title: enterprise-contract-signoff-observability-and-privacy-acceptance-checklist-2026
author: Sophie Chen
body:
Overview:
This checklist documents the minimum observability and privacy acceptance criteria required for enterprise contract signoff and go-live for Dedicated and Private deployments. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Security, and the customer's technical representatives. The goal is to provide a repeatable, testable set of assertions and handoff steps so that contractual SLOs, data residency, telemetry, and privacy obligations are demonstrably met before commercial acceptance.

Scope:
- Applies to: Dedicated, Private (VPC and on-prem) and hybrid tenants where the customer contract requires explicit observability and privacy signoff.
- Not in scope: self-serve hosted API free-tier signups unless contractually required.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) / Onboarding Engineers
- Security & Compliance reviewers
- Customer Tenant Owners and Architects

Prerequisites (before initiating signoff):
1. Tenant provisioned and networked (ingress + egress tests passed).
2. Telemetry forwarding configured (metrics, traces, logs, and sampling policy).
3. Data classification worksheet completed and customer KMS/HSM keys provisioned if applicable.
4. QBR telemetry dashboard scaffold created in customer-facing Console or linked Grafana.
5. Active test account and representative sample workload defined.

Acceptance Criteria (high-level):
- Operational: 99.9% Request success at p95 latency <= contractual SLO for the provisioned model class under representative load test.
- Observability: End-to-end traces that include request id, model id/version, routing decision, and cost tokens.
- Privacy: No PII exfiltration in telemetry; PII fields are pseudonymized or redacted as per data classification.
- Security: Audit log ingestion (control plane) visible with MFA and role-based approvals recorded.

Telemetry & Observability Contract (table):
- Metric: request_rate_total | Required: yes | Thresholds to validate: baseline and stress | Owner: customer-success/eng-platform
- Metric: token_cost_estimate_per_request | Required: yes | Validate: token accounting matches invoice sample | Owner: finance-legal/customer-success
- Trace span requirements: root span with tenant_id, request_id, model_variant, routing_policy, latency_ms | Sampling: 100% for signoff tests, production default afterwards | Owner: eng-platform
- Logs: request-level logs must omit raw request_text by default; sample redaction policy provided | Owner: security-and-compliance

Telemetry Assertions (must pass automated checks):
1. Request correlation: For a batch of 1,000 synthetic signoff requests, at least 98% of requests must have a complete trace (root + model selection + response generation spans).
2. Token accounting: Sample 200 responses and assert token_count * model_unit_price within +/- 3% of invoice-calculated cost for the same window.
3. Error classification: >= 95% of 429 and 5xx errors are attributable to documented root causes (quota, model-unavailable, network); unmapped errors require engineering triage.
4. PII leakage scan: Run the configured PII detector on 1,000 logged fields; zero instances of high-confidence PII stored in telemetry outputs.

Signoff Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff meeting: Owner (CSM) schedules signoff review with SE, SRE, Security, Finance rep, and customer technical lead. Share signoff checklist and test harness two business days in advance.
2. Run the telemetry smoke tests: SE runs the automated signoff suite (links in Related Tools) that validates traces, metrics, and log redaction.
3. Confirm network and ingress: Verify TLS termination, client certs (if used), and firewall rules using the ingress checklist (see commands below).
4. Execute load slice: Run representative workload for 30 minutes at customer peak * 1.2 factor; capture p50/p95/p99 latency and success rate.
5. Privacy validation: Security runs PII detector job and verifies pseudonymization/redaction artifacts.
6. Finance reconciliation: Share sample invoice window for test period and validate token accounting assertion.
7. Signoff meeting: Present results, open action items, and obtain formal acceptance from customer technical approver and Redwood legal/finance approval if any commercial contingencies exist.
8. Document acceptance: CSM updates the customer onboarding record with artifacts and marks the contract milestone as "observability & privacy accepted".

Roles & Responsibilities:
- CSM: coordinate schedule, runbook ownership, and customer communications.
- SE / Onboarding Engineer: execute the test harness, run load scenarios, collect artifacts, and remediate integration issues.
- Eng-Platform: ensure tracing and metrics endpoints meet schema and retention requirements.
- Security: validate PII handling, KMS integration, and audit logging.
- Finance-Legal: confirm that sampled telemetry cost calculations align to invoicing model and advise on any commercial holdbacks.

Test Scenarios (minimum):
1. Baseline functional: 1000 low-concurrency requests (cold start coverage) to assert correct routing and model_variant tagging.
2. Peak-surge: 30-minute run at 120% planned peak to validate autoscaling and latency SLOs.
3. Failover: Simulate model variant unavailability and verify automatic fallback to the contracted model class and correct audit events.
4. Privacy edge-case: Submit requests containing synthetic PII patterns and confirm detectors trigger and telemetry does not store raw PII.

Troubleshooting and Remediation Guidance:
- Missing traces: Verify client instrumentation header (X-Request-Id) propagation, ingress proxy sampling override, and trace-collector connectivity.
- Token accounting mismatch: Re-run tokenization locally with the same model/tooling, compare log token_count to billed tokens, escalate to finance if mismatch > 5%.
- PII found in logs: Immediately rotate the ingest pipeline to redact and re-ingest; start an incident with SRE and Security, notify customer per contract.

Rollback / Pause Go-Live (escape hatch):
- Criteria to pause: sustained p95 latency breach > SLA for 15 consecutive minutes, token accounting variance > 5% with unknown root cause, or confirmed PII exposure.
- Immediate actions: 1) Flip tenant to pre-approved fallback model variant or lower throughput mode; 2) Engage continent on-call SRE; 3) Open customer incident and follow escalation matrix below.

Escalation Matrix (contacts & SLAs):
- First-line: Customer Solutions Engineer (1h response) -> CSM (2h)
- Second-line: Eng-Platform on-call (30m pager) -> SRE (1h)
- Security incident: Security on-call (15m pager) -> Head of Security (1h)
- Finance disputes: Finance-Legal (4 business hours)

Artifacts to Attach to Signoff Record:
- Tracing export (zip) for signoff window
- Aggregated latency and error metrics (CSV)
- PII detector report and remediation notes
- Sample invoice reconciliation worksheet
- Network ingress/egress test logs and firewall rule snapshots

Example commands and snippets:
- Ingress connectivity test (curl):
  curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key "https://tenant-ingress.redwood.example/v1/health"

- Trace sampling check (curl to internal trace endpoint):
  curl -H "X-Request-Id: signoff-test-123" "https://observability.redwood.example/api/v1/trace?request_id=signoff-test-123"

- Minimal telemetry assertion JSON (to feed to signoff harness):
  {
    "tenant_id": "acme-corp-123",
    "test_run": "observability-signoff-2026-03",
    "expected_metrics": ["request_rate_total","token_cost_estimate_per_request"]
  }

Related tools and templates:
- Signoff harness repository: git+ssh://git.redwood/sre/signoff-harness (branch: enterprise-signoff)
- PII detector job: /tools/pii-detector/run-signoff-scan
- Signoff meeting template (Confluence): /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/qbr-template-and-operational-checklist-2026

Post-signoff: Monitoring and QBR handover:
- After formal signoff, SE schedules a 30-day stabilization window with weekly check-ins.
- CSM ensures the QBR dashboard includes the signoff metrics and a recurring telemetry health check (synthetic tests) with alerts routed to the customer’s on-call.
- Any open action items must be tracked as Jira stories with "onboarding:observability-acceptance" label and resolved before final invoicing milestone.

Appendix: Acceptance signature template (copy into Confluence meeting notes):
- Customer technical approver: NAME / TITLE / EMAIL / DATE
- Redwood technical approver (SE): NAME / TITLE / EMAIL / DATE
- Redwood legal/finance approver: NAME / TITLE / EMAIL / DATE
- Observability signoff artifacts attached: [tracing.zip] [metrics.csv] [pii-report.pdf]

Notes and rationale:
This checklist separates operational acceptance concerns (latency, errors) from contractually sensitive privacy and billing assertions. It is intentionally conservative for the first enterprise tenants; subsequent customers may see some checks relaxed after repeated proven runs. Always retain signoff artifacts as legal evidence for dispute resolution.
